name: Gabon
system_note: Led by the general who ousted the Bongo dynasty in 2023.
snapshot: The general who ended 56 years of Bongo family rule in a 2023 coup won the 2025 presidential election by a landslide and abolished the post of prime minister.
culture: Gabon's Fang, Punu, Nzebi and other peoples share a strong tradition of Bwiti, a spiritual practice using the iboga root in initiation ceremonies. Gabonese masks, especially the white-faced Punu masks, influenced European modernists. Libreville's music scene blends Congolese rumba with local styles. French is the official and common language.
society: Nearly 90 percent of the country is rainforest, and Gabon has won international payments for protecting it. Oil, manganese and timber earn most export income, but a third of people live in poverty. Most of the population lives in Libreville and Port-Gentil.
situation: General Brice Clotaire Oligui Nguema, head of the Republican Guard, seized power in August 2023 after Ali Bongo was declared winner of a disputed election. A new constitution approved in 2024 created a strong presidency without a prime minister, and Oligui won the April 2025 election with about 90 percent. His party then won the most seats in the first legislative elections since the coup, held in two rounds in late 2025 amid complaints of irregularities. Oligui has billed 2026 as a year of delivery on roads, power and jobs.
power: A presidential republic under the 2024 constitution: the president is head of state and government, elected for seven years and renewable once, and governs with a vice-president of the government instead of a prime minister.

leaders.state: President Brice Clotaire Oligui Nguema, since 2023
